answer_text:
Here is a breakdown of the maximum unemployment benefits you can collect in Massachusetts in 2026:

### 💰 Maximum Weekly Benefit Amount
Your weekly benefit amount will be about **50% of your average weekly wage**, up to the maximum amount set by law. As of **October 5, 2025, the maximum weekly benefit amount is $1,105 per week.**

### 👨‍👧 Dependency Allowance
If you have any dependents and you are their main support, you may be eligible for a **dependency allowance of up to $25 per child**. Spouses are not included.

### 📅 Maximum Duration
The **maximum duration of benefits is 30 weeks** in Massachusetts. Under normal conditions, the duration is **26 weeks**.

### 💵 Maximum Total Payout
The total maximum payout — combining the weekly rate with the maximum duration — is highest in Massachusetts at approximately **$33,150** (30 weeks × $1,105).

### 📋 Quick Summary Table

| Detail | Amount |
|---|---|
| Max Weekly Benefit | $1,105/week |
| Additional Per Dependent Child | Up to $25/week |
| Standard Duration | 26 weeks |
| Maximum Duration | 30 weeks |
| Max Total Payout | ~$33,150 |

### 🏆 How Massachusetts Compares
Massachusetts is one of the most generous states in the country, with a maximum of **$1,105 per week (with dependents)** and **$823 without dependents**.

### 💼 Taxes
Unemployment benefits are taxable for both **federal and Massachusetts state income tax** purposes. You can elect to have **10% withheld for federal taxes** and **5% withheld for Massachusetts state taxes**.

For the most up-to-date information, you can visit the official Massachusetts DUA website at **mass.gov**.
